module.purpose: Exports the useAtom React hook function with multiple TypeScript overloads for type-safe atom state access and mutation in Jotai.
module.summary: A React hook that provides read and write access to atoms with full TypeScript type inference. It uses function overloads to differentiate between PrimitiveAtom, WritableAtom, and abstract Atom types, returning appropriate tuple types. The implementation delegates to useAtomValue for reading and useSetAtom for writing, with a deliberate type assertion that may trigger type errors.
module.businessContext: Part of Jotai, a primitive and flexible state management library for React. This hook is the primary interface for consuming atoms in React components. If broken, all React-based atom usage fails.
functions: useAtom (~L17-56): React hook for atom state access and mutation with type-safe overloads

export function useAtom<
  AtomType extends WritableAtom<unknown, never[], unknown>,
>(
  atom: AtomType,
  options?: Options,
): [
    Awaited<ExtractAtomValue<AtomType>>,
    SetAtom<ExtractAtomArgs<AtomType>, ExtractAtomResult<AtomType>>,
  ]

detail.name: useAtom
detail.signature: export function useAtom<Value, Args extends unknown[], Result>(atom: Atom<Value> | WritableAtom<Value, Args, Result>, options?: Options): [Value, (...args: Args) => Result]
preconditions: Must be called within a React component or custom hook context
atom must be a valid Atom or WritableAtom instance
postconditions: Returns a two-element tuple where the first element is the current atom value and the second is its setter function
The returned value re-renders on atom state changes
The setter dispatches to useSetAtom for the given atom
edgeCases: When a read-only Atom<Value> is passed, the return type still claims a setter exists; invoking that setter will throw at runtime because useSetAtom receives a non-writable atom via an unsound cast
When options is omitted, both useAtomValue and useSetAtom receive undefined for options

errorPolicy.onInvalidInput: Throws at runtime if useSetAtom is invoked on a non-writable atom (unsound type assertion allows compilation but fails at call time)

detail.summary: Convenience React hook that combines useAtomValue and useSetAtom, returning a [value, setter] tuple for the given atom. A read-only atom passed as a writable atom will cause the setter to throw at runtime due to an intentional unsound type assertion.

specTests.then: Returns a tuple where the first element is 0 and the second element is a function that, when called with a number, updates the atom value

specTests.when: useAtom(readOnlyAtom) is called and the returned setter is invoked with any argument
specTests.then: The call throws at runtime because useSetAtom receives a non-writable atom via an unsound type assertion
The options are forwarded to both useAtomValue and useSetAtom identically
